install.q: Do I need an app store?

data.a: Yes. Download everything as one file whenever you want, and delete your account completely at any time.

meta.title: Pricing — Free and Pro — Sunnsteel
meta.description: Training is free. Pro adds planning depth, longer history and the AI tools for {price} a month, with {days} days free.

pricing.heading: Free to train. Pro to plan further.
pricing.subline: Everything you do in a workout is free. Pro adds planning depth, longer history and the AI tools.

free.heading: Is it free?
free.body: Yes: logging, progression, history, records, ranks and everything social are free, with no card.

compare.heading: Free and Pro, row by row

who.heading: Who Pro is for
who.planners: Lifters who plan blocks and deloads, and want each block's loads set in advance.
who.readers: Lifters who read their training closely: long history, comparisons and signals.
who.ai: Anyone who wants a routine drafted from a description, or a review of their own workouts.

faq.cancel: Yes, from <settings>Settings › Account</settings> or the <cancellation>cancellation page</cancellation>. Nothing renews after that, and you keep Pro until the end of what you paid for, or of the free trial.
faq.trial: An account's first subscription starts with {days} days free. Mercado Pago checks your card without charging it, and the first charge comes when the trial ends; cancel before then and nothing is charged.
faq.refund: Within {days} days of subscribing you can revoke the purchase from the <revocation>revocation page</revocation>, with no reason needed, and what was charged is refunded. The <refunds>refund policy</refunds> has the details.
faq.charge: Mercado Pago charges {price} each month to the card or account you choose on its page. Sunnsteel never sees your card.

outcomes.plan: Dated training blocks, planned deloads and 8-week blocks that set each week's loads.
outcomes.compare: Compare blocks and sessions, read your training signals, get goal suggestions and have chosen workouts reviewed from your own data.
outcomes.history: Strength trends past 90 days, muscle history past four weeks and every body measurement.
outcomes.yours: Your dashboard in your order, routine drafts from your own words, and more routine versions, goals and gyms.

meta.title: Workout tracker — Sunnsteel
meta.description: Log every set in seconds: last time beside each set, a rest timer that starts itself, plates and warm-ups worked out. Free.

workoutTracker.heading: Log every set in seconds
workoutTracker.subline: The workout screen shows your last numbers, starts the rest timer, loads the bar for you and keeps going when the signal drops.
workoutTracker.overview: It's built for one hand between sets. Each exercise states today's prescription once, shows what you did last time beside every set, and saves a set the moment you mark it.

last.title: Last time, beside every set
last.body: The weight and reps from your last workout sit next to each set, so you know what to beat.

rest.title: Rest that starts itself
rest.body: Marking a set starts the timer, and with notifications on it tells you when rest is over, even with the screen locked.

plates.title: Plates and warm-ups worked out
plates.body: The plate calculator loads each side from your gym's plates, and warm-ups can follow your working weight.

facts.kinds: {count} set kinds: working, warm-up, drop, optional
facts.extra: Up to {max} extra sets per exercise
facts.corrections: Your latest workout can be corrected for {hours} hours

steps.1: Start today's workout from your dashboard or your schedule.
steps.2: Each exercise shows its prescription once, and your last numbers beside every set.
steps.3: Type the weight and reps and mark the set: it saves at once and the rest timer starts.
steps.4: Swap an exercise, add an extra set or write a note when the day calls for it.
steps.5: Finish and read your recap: totals, records and what moves next time.

example.title: Warm-ups and plates for a 100 kg working set
example.caption: Worked out by the rule the workout screen uses, with a 20 kg bar and a standard set of plates.
example.columns: Step · Weight · Reps · Plates per side

covers.all: Everything in a workout is free.

tips.1: Log the weight you actually lifted: progression reads what you did, not what was planned.
tips.2: Mark a set only when it's done; a skipped set never moves your routine.
tips.3: Training with gloves or chalk? Turn on larger controls in Settings.
tips.4: Use a note for what the numbers can't say.

locked.q: Does the rest alert work with the screen locked?
locked.a: Yes, once notifications are on. On iPhone, notifications need the installed app. The alert says rest is over and what comes next; it doesn't show a countdown.

signal.a: Keep logging. Your sets are sent when the connection returns, as long as the app stays open, and it tells you when changes are waiting.

add.q: Can I add an exercise mid-workout?
add.a: Not a new one: the routine is the plan. You can swap an exercise for today, add extra sets, or change the routine for next time.

fix.q: Can I fix a finished workout?
fix.a: Your latest one, for {hours} hours and until you start another. Records and progression are worked out again from the corrected sets.

forgot.q: I forgot to log a workout.
forgot.a: You can log a past workout of one of your routines afterwards, with the date and the sets you did.

meta.title: Routine builder — Sunnsteel
meta.description: Build weekly or rotating routines from scratch or a template, with a summary of weekly sets, duration and equipment. Drafts from a description on Pro.

routineBuilder.heading: Build the routine you'll actually follow
routineBuilder.subline: Weekly or rotating, from scratch or a template, with a summary that tells you what each week adds up to before you save it.
routineBuilder.overview: A routine is your plan: its days, each day's exercises, and for each exercise its sets, reps, rest and how it progresses. Everything you train starts here.

schedule.title: Weekly or rotation
schedule.body: Train on set weekdays, or run your days in order on any day you train.

templates.title: Start from a template
templates.body: {count} programs open as drafts, with every weight left for you to fill in.

summary.title: Know what you planned
summary.body: Weekly sets per muscle, an estimated length for each day and the equipment it needs, before you save.

facts.versions: {free} saved versions on Free, {pro} on Pro
facts.custom: Up to {max} exercises of your own
facts.drafts: {count} routine drafts a month on Pro

steps.1: Choose weekly or rotation, and your training days.
steps.2: Add exercises from the catalog, or create your own.
steps.3: Set sets, reps or a rep range, rest, and how each exercise progresses.
steps.4: Link exercises into supersets or circuits if you train them in rounds.
steps.5: Read the summary and create it. Nothing is saved until you do.

example.title: What Upper / Lower plans each week
example.caption: Weekly sets per muscle, counted as the app counts them: each set counts 1 for a primary muscle and 0.5 for a secondary one.

draft.heading: Describe it, get a draft
draft.body: Tell it what you want -- days, goal, equipment -- and a draft opens in the builder, every weight left blank. Your text goes to Anthropic to write the draft and isn't stored. It's a starting point, not medical advice.

covers.rows: Weekly and rotating routines · templates · your own exercises: Free and Pro. Saved versions: {free} / {pro}. Routine drafts: Pro, {drafts} a month. Training blocks and 8-week blocks: Pro.

tips.1: Leave weights blank on a new routine: your first workout sets them.
tips.2: Train on different days each week? Use a rotation.
tips.3: Save a version before a big change; you can compare it and restore it later.

rotation.a: Days that run in order whenever you train, instead of on fixed weekdays. A missed day doesn't get skipped: the next one waits for you.

share.q: Can I share or copy a routine?
share.a: Yes. Share it with a link or on your profile, and anyone allowed to see it can copy it into their own routines. A copy is independent: your training never travels with it.

versions.q: How many versions can I keep?
versions.a: {free} per routine on Free and {pro} on Pro. Older versions you already have are kept.

draft.a: Only the text you write, to Anthropic, to write the draft; it isn't stored. The draft arrives with no weights, and nothing is saved until you create the routine.

meta.title: Automatic progression — Sunnsteel
meta.description: Double progression moves your weights from what you actually lift. With Pro, 8-week blocks set each week's load from a reference max.

progression.heading: The weight goes up when you earn it
progression.subline: Double progression moves your weights from what you actually lift. With Pro, an 8-week block sets every week's load from a reference max.
progression.overview: Each exercise chooses how it progresses. Most progress by double progression: work up the rep range at one weight, then add weight. The app does the arithmetic at the end of each workout, from the sets you marked done.

double.title: Double progression
double.body: When every set reaches the top of its range, the next workout adds one step.

perSet.title: Set by set, if you prefer
perSet.body: Dynamic double progression moves each set on its own.

block.title: 8-week blocks
block.body: Eight weeks of loads from a reference max, ending in an estimate of your new max.

facts.schemes: Double, set by set, 8-week block or none
facts.block: A block is {weeks} weeks, {sets} working sets a week

steps.1: Give the exercise a rep range, such as 8–12, and a step.
steps.2: Train, and mark each set with the weight and reps you did.
steps.3: When every working set reaches the top of the range, the next workout's weight rises by the step.
steps.4: If they don't, the weight you lifted stays, and you work up the range again.

example.title: Double progression on 3 × 8–12, workout by workout
example.caption: Bench Press with a 2.5 kg step, checked against the rule the server applies.

block.heading: An 8-week block from a 100 kg reference max
block.caption: Three working sets a week at the week's share of your reference max, rounded to your step. Weeks 1–4 keep 2–3 reps in reserve and end with a set of as many good reps as you can; weeks 5–8 keep 1–2 in reserve.
block.columns: Week · Share · Load · Reps in reserve
block.amrap: As many good reps as you can

covers.rows: Double and set-by-set progression: Free and Pro. 8-week blocks and planned deloads: Pro.

tips.1: Pick a step your gym can load: 2.5 kg on a barbell, less where you have smaller plates.
tips.2: Log the reps you really did; rounding up moves the weight before you're ready.
tips.3: A swapped exercise never moves the prescription, so swapping is safe.

miss.q: What if I miss my reps?
miss.a: The weight you lifted carries over and nothing goes up. Work up the range again at that weight.

off.q: Can I switch it off for one exercise?
off.a: Yes. Each exercise has its own setting, and "None" keeps its weights where you put them.

step.a: The one you set for the exercise, {step} unless you choose another.

deload.q: Does a deload move my weights?
deload.a: No. Progression pauses for deload workouts, so the plan you lightened keeps its weights.

meta.title: Progress — Sunnsteel
meta.description: Strength trends, a body map of weekly sets, records and body weight, each with the number behind it. Signals, comparisons and reviews on Pro.

progress.heading: Progress you can read
progress.subline: Strength, muscles, records and body weight, each with the number behind it, and analysis that states what changed, never why.
progress.overview: Everything here is read from the sets you logged. Every chart says what it counts, and every flag prints the rule that raised it.

strength.title: Strength over time
strength.body: Your estimated 1RM per exercise, with every record that moved it.

map.title: The body map
map.body: Weekly sets per muscle, front and back, beside the number behind each color.

plateaus.title: Plateau watch
plateaus.body: Lifts with no new best after several sessions, with the rule written above them.

facts.strength: Strength history: {days} days on Free, longer on Pro
facts.muscles: Muscle history: {free} weeks on Free, {pro} on Pro
facts.reviews: Training reviews: {count} a month on Pro

steps.1: Log your workouts; records are found in your sets as you go.
steps.2: Read strength by exercise, and each exercise's own page with its history.
steps.3: Check the body map each week to see where your sets went.
steps.4: Let plateau watch tell you which lifts have stopped setting bests.
steps.5: With Pro, compare blocks and sessions, read your training signals and ask for a review.

example.title: How one workout lands on the body map
example.caption: Bench Press, 3 working sets: each set counts 1 for its primary muscles and 0.5 for its secondary ones; warm-ups don't count.

covers.rows: Records, plateau watch, body weight: Free and Pro. Strength trends: {days} days / longer. Body map: {free} weeks / {pro}. Goals: {freeGoals} / {proGoals}. Body measurements beyond weight, training signals and the deload suggestion, comparisons, goal suggestions, training reviews: Pro.

tips.1: Log RPE on your hard sets to see effort in signals and reviews.
tips.2: Weigh yourself in the same conditions each time for a cleaner line.
tips.3: A plateau flag is a fact to look at, not a verdict.

e1rm.a: The heaviest single rep a set suggests, worked out from its weight and reps. It's an estimate, not a lift you tried.

bodyweight.q: Why don't bodyweight sets add volume?
bodyweight.a: Volume is the load you added times the reps. A bodyweight set counts as a set but adds no load.

signals.q: Do signals tell me what's wrong?
signals.a: No. They show what changed, with the numbers and the rule; the reason is yours to judge.

pro.a: Longer history, body measurements beyond weight, training signals and the deload suggestion, comparisons, goal suggestions and training reviews.

meta.title: Ranks and achievements — Sunnsteel
meta.description: {ranks} ranks and {milestones} milestones earned by training, comebacks recognized, and records found in your sets. Free.

ranks.heading: Earned by showing up
ranks.subline: {ranks} ranks and {milestones} milestones, earned from your workouts, and records found in your sets. Nothing here is for posting.
ranks.overview: A rank rewards attendance: workouts across different weeks. Milestones mark totals you reach. Records are detected from your sets the moment you set one.

ranks.title: {ranks} ranks
ranks.body: From {first} to {last}, each with its crest, earned by workouts in different weeks.

milestones.title: {milestones} milestones
milestones.body: Workouts, sets, volume, records and streaks, each in steps.

comebacks.title: Comebacks
comebacks.body: Time away is never punished: coming back is recognized.

facts.comeback: A comeback: {active} active days within {window} days, after {away} days away
facts.featured: Feature up to {max} accomplishments on your profile

steps.1: Train: every week you work out counts as an active week, however many workouts it holds.
steps.2: Reach a rank's workouts and active weeks, and the rank is yours.
steps.3: Milestones arrive as your totals cross them.
steps.4: Choose who sees your rank, and feature what you're proud of on your profile.

example.title: The ladder and the milestones
example.caption: Read from the app's own catalog.

covers.all: Ranks, milestones, comebacks and records are free.

tips.1: Consistency beats bursts: three weeks with one workout each count more toward a rank than one week with three.
tips.2: Don't chase a streak at the cost of rest; the milestones will wait.

earned.a: By a number of workouts spread over a number of different weeks; both have to be met.

comeback.a: After {away} days or more without training, {active} active days within {window} days record a comeback.

who.a: You choose: everyone, your followers, or only you.

records.a: Yes, from your sets, as you train. If you correct a workout, its records are worked out again.

meta.title: Training with people — Sunnsteel
meta.description: Follow people, train with partners and send what you trained, with each part of your profile shown only to whom you choose. Free.

community.heading: Train with people, on your terms
community.subline: Follow, train with partners and send what you trained, with each part of your profile shown only to whom you choose.
community.overview: Your activity comes from what you train, not from posts. Followers see what you let them; partners see what you grant; messages carry the real thing.

activity.title: Activity
activity.body: Workouts, records and milestones from people you follow, with {reactions} reactions and comments.

partners.title: Training partners
partners.body: Up to {max} partners, each choosing what the other sees, with an alert when a partner finishes a workout if you want one.

messages.title: Messages
messages.body: One to one, carrying a routine, a workout, a record, a milestone, a comeback or a month of training.

facts.privacy: {count} parts of your profile, each with its own audience

steps.1: Follow people you train with or admire.
steps.2: See their workouts, records and milestones, and react or comment.
steps.3: Become training partners and choose what each of you sees.
steps.4: Send a routine, a workout or a record in a message, or share a workout with a link.

example.title: Your profile, part by part
example.caption: Each part has its own audience: Everyone, Followers or Only me.

covers.all: Everything social, and messages, is free.

tips.1: Set each part of your profile once in Settings; you can change it any time.
tips.2: A share link shows only the parts you pick, and you can revoke it.

encrypted.a: No. They're stored on our servers. A moderator reads a message only if it's reported, and then only that message and up to {context} before it.

who.a: You choose: people you follow, everyone (people you don't follow arrive as requests), or nobody.

share.q: Can I share a workout with someone without an account?
share.a: Yes, with a link that shows only the parts you pick. You can revoke it, and it stops working at once.

blocks.q: How do blocks and reports work?
blocks.a: A block hides you from each other everywhere and removes follows both ways. A report goes to a moderator, who reads only what it's about.

meta.title: Sunnsteel for beginners
meta.description: A full-body program three days a week, the weights worked out for you, and progress you can see from the first month.

beginners.heading: Start lifting with a plan
beginners.subline: A full-body program three days a week, the weights worked out for you, and progress you can see from the first month.
beginners.audience: For anyone in their first months of lifting
beginners.facts: 3 days a week · Full body · Free

1.title: Learn a few movements well
1.body: A short list of exercises, repeated, teaches them faster than variety.

2.title: Your first weights are yours to find
2.body: Templates leave every weight blank; your first workout sets them.

3.title: Add weight when you've earned it
3.body: When every set reaches the top of its range, the next workout adds a step.

4.title: Show up most weeks
4.body: Ranks reward workouts across different weeks, not long sessions.

steps.1: Create a free account and tell it your days and goals.
steps.2: Start with Full Body Foundations, or the program it recommends.
steps.3: In your first workout, find a weight you can do with good form for the low end of each range.
steps.4: Train three days a week; let progression move the weights.
steps.5: When plateau watch flags a lift for weeks, read the intermediates' page.

gym.a: Full Body Foundations uses common gym equipment. You can build your own routine for what you have, and your gym's plates are saved for the plate calculator.

weights.q: How do I know my starting weights?
weights.a: Your first workout finds them: pick a weight you can do with good form at the low end of the range, and log it.

meta.title: Sunnsteel for intermediates
meta.description: Split your week, track weekly sets per muscle and read your plateaus as numbers, not guesses.

intermediates.heading: Keep progressing past the first months
intermediates.subline: Split your week, track weekly sets per muscle and read your plateaus as numbers, not guesses.
intermediates.audience: For lifters whose first program has stopped moving
intermediates.facts: 4 to 6 days a week · Upper/lower or push/pull/legs · Free

1.title: Progress slows
1.body: Adding weight every week stops; a range takes longer to climb.

2.title: Split the body
2.body: Upper/lower or push/pull/legs give each muscle more weekly sets.

3.title: Weekly sets become the measure
3.body: How many sets each muscle gets in a week matters more than any single workout.

4.title: Plateaus are read, not guessed
4.body: A lift that stops setting bests is flagged with its numbers.

steps.1: Choose Upper / Lower or Push / Pull / Legs, or build your own split.
steps.2: Use your current weights as the new routine's starting weights.
steps.3: Check the body map weekly and adjust sets where a muscle falls short.
steps.4: Save a version before each change, so you can compare.
steps.5: When a lift stalls for weeks, try an 8-week block (Pro).

intermediates.next: Ready for blocks and deloads? Advanced

split.a: Upper / Lower is four days on set weekdays; Push / Pull / Legs is a rotation, each day twice a week. Choose the one that fits the days you have.

meta.title: Sunnsteel for advanced lifters
meta.description: 8-week blocks from a reference max, planned deloads, and comparisons that put each block beside the one before.

advanced.heading: Plan blocks, deloads and the long game
advanced.subline: 8-week blocks from a reference max, planned deloads, and comparisons that put each block beside the one before.
advanced.audience: For lifters who plan their training in blocks

1.title: Training runs in blocks
1.body: Weeks are planned in advance, each with its own load.

2.title: Deloads are planned, not improvised
2.body: A lighter week goes on the calendar before you need it.

3.title: Blocks are compared
3.body: Each block sits beside the one before, with its numbers and no verdict.

4.title: Signals are read over weeks
4.body: Effort, rep targets and declines, two weeks against the two before.

steps.1: Build your routine, or start from a template you'll change.
steps.2: Give your main lifts an 8-week block from a reference max.
steps.3: Plan a deload where the block calls for one.
steps.4: At the end of the block, read the estimate and choose what comes next.
steps.5: Compare the block with the one before, and ask for a review of the workouts you choose.

template.a: No: advanced training is yours to build. The builder, the 8-week block and deloads are where you build it.
